kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: the near-floor control must self-negate — zero unique detections against the executed scripted conventional test

expected.detail: the control fixture has one subject and one observer; the coherence equation subject∘event = seen fails on Observer row 0 (delivered e2, current e1). The scripted conventional test checks notification coverage and payload coherence for the single observer, so it catches the same element. Unique must be empty for the control to self-negate.

comparison.conventional_baseline: scripted Observer test over the single-observer/subject fixture: the observer has a delivered event and it equals event(subject(observer)); the floor model is fully covered by that check

expressibility_gap.invariant: notification totality over dynamically registered observers
expressibility_gap.why: the model names the observer rows and subject edges up front; registration changes are outside the check

discrepancies: ploeh-grounding.md §6 lists these patterns as HYPOTHESIZED candidates, not proven equivalences; this slice records parity or a null result and does not upgrade any of them.
procedure: 1. control first: validate the near-floor control's empty unique set and killed verdict before any positive is read.
2. probe arm: cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check <fixture> --json; findings recorded verbatim.
3. baseline arm: python3 prototype/weak_lens_set_baseline.py --assert; detections are the pre-registered element names.
4. unique = probe elements - baseline elements; the element vocabulary is fixed in fixtures/katas/weak-lens-set/README.md.
5. verdict: empty unique with an expressible lens => killed (parity); an unexpressible lens with zero findings => killed with the gap recorded (null result).
